headline: High: Roo Code can write shared workspace files and use MCP/browser, creating medium-to-high risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors with TREK's collaborative travel data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and can use MCP, while TREK is a real-time collaborative app with MCP and browser surfaces. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path if TREK content is opened in the workspace or passed through MCP. The interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF TREK content is copied into a VS Code workspace file that Roo Code reads
IF either agent routes MCP payloads without provenance tags
mitigations: Separate TREK artifacts from Roo Code workspaces
Disable MCP endpoints not needed for the task
Require explicit human review before acting on file content
Add provenance labels to any shared notes or prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code has broad network egress and handles model provider API keys; TREK touches reservations, documents, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets. If TREK data enters Roo Code's workspace, Roo Code can transmit it to third-party model APIs by default, making leakage plausible and potentially severe. The pairwise path is indirect but credible.
conditions: IF TREK secrets or reservation data are placed in files Roo Code can read
IF Roo Code sends those files to a configured model provider API
mitigations: Keep TREK secrets out of shared workspace files
Use a local-only model for Roo Code when handling TREK data
Redact confirmation numbers and API keys before review
Restrict Roo Code network access during TREK tasks
Rotate any exposed secrets immediately

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands in a per-workspace session; TREK is collaborative and stores data in files and logs. Shared filesystem state plus concurrent instances creates a real write-conflict pathway, and the rubric treats overlapping unrestricted writes as high risk when locks are absent. TREK's collaborative model increases the chance of concurrent mutation.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or data directory
IF concurrent edits occur without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches and explicit merge review
Enable file locking or transactional writes
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can generate code, edits, and browser-driven outputs, while TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in. If TREK consumes Roo Code's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect travel plans, reservations, or user-facing actions. The default collaborative setup makes this pathway plausible without extra safeguards.
conditions: IF TREK ingests Roo Code output without verification
IF Roo Code-generated text is used to update reservations or plans
mitigations: Require a verification step before TREK acts on Roo Code output
Limit Roo Code to draft-only suggestions
Log source attribution for every imported field
Block automatic reservation or email actions from unreviewed text

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly touches reservations, documents, email addresses, country visit history, and secrets, while Roo Code handles browser screenshots and model-provider API keys in a VS Code workspace. If EU PII or travel documents flow from TREK into Roo Code's third-party model calls, residency and retention obligations can be breached. The profiles do not show a DPA or residency control, so uncertainty escalates to high.
conditions: IF TREK data includes EU PII or travel documents
IF Roo Code forwards that data to a non-EU model provider or logs it externally
mitigations: Keep regulated travel data out of Roo Code prompts
Use a residency-approved model endpoint
Disable external logging for shared sessions
Review retention settings before processing documents
Pseudonymize traveler identifiers before analysis
